short: Capped energies and the 1 mHa RMS bound

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.p450GroundEnergy_correctness
lean.plain: Energy error of the compiled circuit
lean.annotation: For each disjoint register placement, the decoder is fixed and the theorem supplies a unitary $W$. The first conjunct gives the error bound on all the qualifying eigenstates with that $W$. The second conjunct relates the same $W$ to the compiled program with zero-initialized ancillas.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.MeasuresLowEnergies
lean.plain: RMS error after capping both energies
lean.annotation: For a supplied normalized eigenstate with E ≥ T, the capped loss is max(T − Ê, 0)², so a decoded estimate at least 10 mHa below T occurs with probability at most 1%. If E ≤ T − 10 mHa, the same squared-loss bound gives at most 1% probability that the uncapped estimate differs from E by 10 mHa or more in either direction.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.PhaseDecoder.energy
lean.plain: Energy from bits of the phase register
lean.annotation: `PhaseDecoder.energy` extracts the phase index from the ancilla outcome and uses |cos(θ/2)|, which is insensitive to the sign and 2π wrap of the doubled phase θ. With exact DFTHC phase information this gives E_off − |E − E_off|, so an energy above E_off is reflected to 2E_off − E and remains at or above a cutoff T only if E ≤ 2E_off − T.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.TightGapDeep63.p450RefVarBound_tightGapDeep63
lean.plain: Variational upper bound on the cutoff
lean.annotation: The Lean theorem bounds any cutoff T satisfying T ≤ E′ + 0.1 Ha for every nonzero eigenvector of the fixed Hamiltonian in the 63-electron sector: T ≤ −130.0526 Ha. This is a one-sided cutoff bound, not an exact ground energy or a proof that the circuit and decoder achieve 1 mHa RMS error.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.p450GroundEnergy_correctness
lean.plain: Energy error of the compiled circuit
lean.annotation: The arguments `63 0.1 0.001` specify the electron number, the window width in Ha, and the RMS tolerance in Ha. The theorem uses the same unitary `W` for the measurement guarantee and for the compiled program’s basis-outcome realization with zero-initialized workspace.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.MeasuresLowEnergies
lean.plain: RMS error after capping both energies
lean.annotation: A cutoff $T$ is admissible when $T\le E'+\Delta$ for every 63-electron eigenvalue $E'$. This is equivalent to $T\le E_0+\Delta$. After both energies are capped at the largest cutoff, applying $x\mapsto\min(x,T)$ to them can only decrease their absolute difference.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.MeasuresLowEnergies
lean.plain: RMS error after capping both energies
lean.annotation: An input-independent capped estimate would have RMS distance at most 1 mHa from both $E_0$ and $E_0+\Delta$. The triangle inequality would give $\Delta\le2$ mHa, while $\Delta=100$ mHa. This instance has an above-window eigenvalue. Averaging the one-body term over the sector and using the nonnegative squares gives a mean sector energy of at least −111.655 Ha, above the cutoff bound of −130.0526 Ha.
